title: CPlane burnup & rate-limit playtest notes (standup sync)
content:
Meeting: Platform Engineering — control plane / routing / auth playtest
Date: 2026-03-22 09:30 PT (standup slot)
Facilitator: Lina Chen
Attendees: Lina Chen, Diego Morales, Asha Patel, Brooke Simmons, Omar Rahman (SRE async)

Purpose:
- Run a focused playtest of recent rate-limit and routing fallback changes against a realistic burnup replay.
- Capture p50/p95/p99 latency, throttles, and any auth failures during spike.
- Decide short-term config tweaks and triage follow-ups for rolling out to Dedicated.

Quick TL;DR:
- Replay: 10m warmup + 30m increasing QPS burnup (~200 -> 2,500 RPS peak) using k6 replay harness.
- Observed: p95 token-gen latency increased ~170ms compared to baseline at mid-burn (1,200 RPS), p99 windows hit at peak with 3.8% requests throttled by route-level quota.
- Auth: no signature failures; one transient oauth token-exchange retry (round-trip +600ms) attributed to long-tail KMS call on the key node.
- Routing fallback: automatic fallback to model-shard-secondary worked in 12/12 simulated node outages.
- Decision: reduce default token-bucket refill from 1000/s -> 800/s for lower-cost tiers; add telemetry to differentiate per-route burst vs sustained throttles.

Context / why this test
- PLTFRM-4821 implements burst-aware token buckets and a new global quota controller that can offload to a rate-limit pod group. Before we promote to Dedicated, we need to validate behavior on our most common traffic shape: ramping burst leading to sustained high QPS with KV-cache-hit variance.
- This doc captures raw notes from the standup/playtest and concrete action items.

Test setup:
- Replay harness: infra/loadtests/k6/replays/burnup-2026-03-22.json (scripted user sessions, value of prefix caching varied)
- Cluster: staging-cplane-6 (4 x a100 + 3 x cpu pool for control plane), net emulation default (no artificial loss)
- Configs applied:
  - routing: route-defaults.yaml (token_bucket: capacity=2000, refill=1000/s, burst=3k) -> toggled to refill=800 for candidate test.
  - quotas: global-quota-controller v2 (experimental) enabled on 10% of requests via sampling flag.
  - auth: oauth-cache TTL=3s -> 2s for exercise of token-refresh behavior.
- Commands used:
  - kubectl -n cplane apply -f experiments/rate-limit/playtest-configs/
  - k6 run replays/burnup-2026-03-22.js --vus 200 --duration 40m
  - ./scripts/collect-metrics.sh staging-cplane-6 > /tmp/metrics-2026-03-22.log

Observations (chronological)
1) Warmup (0-10m)
- System warmed as expected; KV cache hit rate ~78% on text generation requests (matching baseline).
- p50 token latency steady at ~22ms.

2) Mid-burn (10-26m, 200 -> 1,200 RPS ramp)
- p95 token latency increased from baseline 240ms -> 410ms. Investigation: increased scheduler queueing in token-gen service due to token-bucket owner mutex contention.
- One observed spike (1 minute window) where route auth latency spiked to p99=1.2s; traced to a KMS node performing HSM-backed key rotation. Correlated with oauth-cache TTL=3s causing near-simultaneous refreshes.

3) Peak (26-40m, 1,200 -> 2,500 RPS)
- 3.8% of requests hit route-level throttle (token-bucket exhausted) during sustained peak; majority were non-privileged tiers.
- Backpressure ripple: downstream serving runtime (gpu-pools) saw higher retry rate; control plane issued automated fallback to model-shard-secondary for routes with configured fallbackPolicy: degrade->secondary. All fallback rollouts completed within 900ms median.
- p99 latency for route resolution climbed to 1.6s at peak.

Errors and anomalies
- 7 oauth token-exchange failures (0.003% overall) observed; 6 recovered via client retries. One remained and required manual reset of cached key; cause: KMS rotation out-of-sync for one key replica.
- Metrics pipeline lag: Prometheus pushed with 40s lag during peak because of scrape contention; some alerting evaluated stale values — need to increase scrape parallelism for cplane cluster.

Playtest-specific findings (unique to this run)
- Burst-aware buckets: when refill lowered to 800/s, the observed throttle rate for non-privileged routes increased from 1.4% -> 3.8% at peak, but p95 latency improved for privileged routes by ~60ms (less queueing). So there's a tradeoff: stricter refill reduces queue backlog but increases throttle events for heavy clients.
- Global quota-controller sampling (10%) correctly offloaded a subset of flow to the rate-limit pods; offloaded requests experienced consistent TTL extensions but slightly higher p50 (extra 30ms). No request loss.

Small experiments and quick wins
- Bump oauth-cache TTL to 5s during rolling KMS rotations to smooth refresh spikes (temp mitigation).
- Increase token-gen service worker threads from 16 -> 24 in staging; observed p95 improvement ~40-60ms. Plan to A/B this in canary.
- Prometheus: increase scrape thread pool for staging-cplane to avoid 40s lag under high cardinality labels.

Decisions from standup
- Ship: change default refill for "standard" tier from 1000/s -> 800/s (backout window 72h) to reduce queuing on control plane. (owner: Diego Morales, due: 2026-03-25)
- Telemetry: add label rate_limit.cause={burst,sustained,quota} to throttled events to enable post-mortem segmentation. (owner: Brooke Simmons, due: 2026-03-29)
- Observability: create dedicated scrape pool for cplane metrics in prod (proposal doc: Confluence link above). (owner: Lina Chen, due: 2026-04-02)

Action items (concrete)
- Diego: prepare rollout PR for default refill change + automated canary gating (PR: GH PR stub created). Due 2026-03-25.
- Brooke: instrument throttles with cause label and publish new dashboard panels for throttle breakdowns (dash ticket: DASH-311). Due 2026-03-29.
- Asha: validate KMS replica sync logic + add forced jitter on oauth-cache TTL during key rotations. Draft playbook update. Due 2026-03-28.
- Omar (SRE): increase Prometheus scrape worker pool for staging and run a 2-hour burnup to validate lag resolution. Due 2026-03-26.
- Lina: schedule canary test for worker-threads bump and capture p95 over 7-day rolling window. Due 2026-03-30.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Tiering semantics: should refill be proportional to committed capacity or to observed tail latency per customer? (Action: Product sync required — link PL product thread)
- Can the global quota controller be made adaptive (auto-scaling offload) rather than sampled? Feasibility assessment requested from infra.
- Need to validate Dedicated customer SLAs under the new refill defaults — risk: some customers on standard tier may see throttles they'd not expect. Suggest contacting 2-3 high-usage customers for heads-up. (owner: customer-success raise)

Notes to self / scratchpad (raw)
- saw ephemeral spike at 10:14am — diff of logs shows KMS rotation event at 10:13:58Z
- quick repro: k6 run -e TARGET=staging-cplane-6 burnup-2026-03-22.js --vus 140 -> reproduce mid-burn characteristics in 12m
- rough costs: increased worker threads bumped CPU by ~15% in staging; estimate prod cost ~+9% if rolled cluster-wide (raise flag)

Meeting artifacts / data dumps
- Raw metrics (gzipped): gs://redwood-playtests/2026-03-22/cplane-burnup-metrics.gz
- Flamegraphs: s3://perf-dumps/2026-03-22/token-gen-flame.svg
- k6 logs: /artifacts/loadtests/burnup-2026-03-22/k6.log

Next sync
- Quick triage checkpoint: 2026-03-24 standup (09:30 PT) to confirm PR stability and canary results.
- Full review with product / cs: 2026-03-30 (15:00 PT) — invite list: product-hosted-api, customer-success reps for any impacted customers.

Appendix: shorthand glossary used here
- token-gen: service that mints request tokens tied to route-level token buckets
- refill: tokens added per second to a bucket
- burst: instantaneous capacity to absorb spikes beyond refill*window
- fallbackPolicy: routing config to degrade to a secondary model/shard when primary unavailable

Scratch/brainstorm (not polished):
- Could introduce per-customer smoothing windows (leaky-bucket across 60s) to avoid single-minute commits causing throttles. But complexity of bookkeeping in global controller increases.
- Alternative: advertise a "burst credit" balance in client SDKs so customers can decide to backoff gracefully (needs API work).

End of notes.

(If anything in here needs immediate follow-up outside the stated action owners, ping me in #pltfm-controlplane — Lina)
